title: The Consensus Trap: Dissecting Subjectivity and the "Ground Truth" Illusion in Data Annotation
findings: The paper finds that the prevailing 'ground truth' paradigm in data annotation systematically erases religious and spiritual contexts from non-Western cultures. This 'geographic hegemony' exports Western communication norms as universal, leading to models that fail in contexts where faith-based sensitivities are crucial. The process of treating disagreement as noise effectively silences these perspectives, as shown in the annotation of datasets on faith-based communal violence.
